title: Everest has its busiest spring ever
text: Nepal issued a record 494 Everest permits in spring 2026, and nearly 900 climbers and guides had summited by the end of the season. The government also raised the Everest royalty from $11,000 to $15,000 per climber.

title: Skiing down Nanga Parbat
text: On 30 June 2026, Polish ski mountaineer Andrzej Bargiel skied from the summit of Nanga Parbat all the way to base camp, without supplemental oxygen. Reports called it a historic moment for the sport.

title: Avalanche on Broad Peak
text: On 30 July 2026, an avalanche struck a ten-member international team on Broad Peak in the Karakoram, and none of the climbers survived. Among them was Nirmal Purja, the Nepali-British mountaineer who was one of the best-known climbers of his generation. The Alpine Club of Pakistan reported on the search and recovery.

title: A summer with no K2 summits
text: Unusually heavy snowfall through much of July made early rope-fixing on K2 extremely difficult, and the summer ended with no successful summits. Across the Karakoram's 8,000-metre peaks, only a handful of climbers reached a summit all season.

title: Himalayan glaciers are melting faster
text: A new report by ICIMOD and the G B Pant National Institute of Himalayan Environment says Himalayan glaciers are melting 65 per cent faster than a decade ago. Retreating glaciers create unstable lakes and slopes, so scientists are calling for better monitoring and early-warning systems.
